question_record.context: A security incident involving a remote session dropping and executing a file named `rubeus.exe` on host `vnevado-win10b` with IP address `141.216.110.153` was detected. This activity is related to the use of the Rubeus kerberoasting tool, designed to exploit Kerberos authentication. The process was executed with command line: `rubeus.exe dump /service:xfbzkp /user:lucasb`, and the incident was traced back to the suspicious account `fk8mq` with Azure AD user ID `97e6a954-b6bd-48a5-808c-bd8464cce677`.
question_record.question: During the investigation, an anomalous chain of attempts to look up user account information was observed. Can you identify the name of the suspicious file associated with this alert?
solution: A file named `rubeus.exe` was dropped and launched from a remote location.

Activity indicating the use of the Rubeus tool, which can perform kerberoasting and other Kerberos authentication attacks, was observed. The suspect account has AadUserId `1d94aaf6-efe6-4e76-ad56-ffd7d1257bc1`.
An anomalous account lookup was performed using the file `domaindominance27.ps1`.

34.name: File dropped and launched from remote location
34.description: A remote session dropped a file and executed it. An attacker or a malware might be an attempting move laterally or propagate.

107.name: Possible use of the Rubeus kerberoasting tool
107.description:
Activity indicating the use of the Rubeus tool was observed on this endpoint. This tool can perform kerberoasting, pass-the-ticket, and other attack techniques that take advantage of Kerberos authentication.

During these attacks, attackers often request Kerberos tickets for an account's service principal name (SPN). They then decrypt the tickets to get plaintext credentials associated with the account. Alternatively, they can perform the pass-the-ticket technique to authenticate directly without having to decrypt the obtained tickets.

94.name: Anomalous account lookups
94.description: An anomalous chain of attempts to look up user account information has been observed. An attacker might be gathering information about potential targets.
